dropped.summary: LOW-8's drop-recording fix is dead on Python 3.13+ and two guards are unconditionally red there; the diff lands two permanently-failing tests on a declared-supported interpreter
dropped.why_refuted:
Mechanism confirmed, scope claim refuted. I reproduced the EACCES control on four interpreters: 3.11.15 and 3.12.13 raise PermissionError from Path.is_dir(), 3.14.4 returns False, and os.stat raises on all four. So ownership.py:385-403's LOW-8 recording is indeed inert on 3.14, and the refusal falls to the generic "no missions were found ... git pull" branch (ownership.py:626-630/:669-673). Suite level: tests/specify_cli/decisions/test_ownership_3111.py is 2 failed, 31 passed on 3.14.4 (both LOW-8 guards, assert () == ('m-link',)), and both files are new in this diff.

But the finding's load-bearing claim is empirically false: 3.13 is NOT affected. python3.13.12 on the identical control gives "is_dir RAISED PermissionError", and the full file is 33 passed on 3.13.12. The cause is source-level, not a patch-build accident: 3.13's pathlib.Path.is_dir still routes through _ignore_error (EACCES not ignored, so it raises), while 3.14 rewrote it to "return os.path.isdir(self)", which swallows every OSError. The divergence begins at 3.14, not 3.13. That collapses the finding's severity argument, which is explicitly anchored on pyproject.toml:40 "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13" being a declared-supported interpreter that is now red — every classifier-declared interpreter (3.11, 3.12, 3.13) is green. 3.14 is only implicitly permitted by requires-python = ">=3.11" and is in no classifier.

Two supporting evidence claims also fail. "every python-version: in ci-quality.yml is '3.12'" is wrong: 48 are '3.12' and 2 are '3.13' (:3848 build-wheel, :3898 clean-install-verification) — the conclusion that no test job sees it survives, the evidence does not. And .python-version pins 3.11.15, so the canonical uv-driven local run is green; "every 3.13+ contributor gets two red tests" is doubly wrong (3.13 contributors get zero, and reaching the 3.14 reds requires deliberately overriding the pinned interpreter). The residual is also already recorded and escalated with the exact fix recipe in follow-ups.md:221-251 (FU-Q) and docs/plans/engineering-notes/01KYW895-verification-evidence.md, and is fail-closed (owned=False, nothing transmits) — diagnosis quality only.

Additional correction: FU-Q's own falsifier ("if is_dir() raised on 3.13+. It does not; probed with a readable control in the same run") is itself untrue — the mission's evidence tables have only 3.11.15 and 3.14.4 columns and claim 3.14 is the only interpreter installed, while uv python find 3.13 resolves 3.13.12. Both the mission note and this finding extrapolated 3.14 backwards onto 3.13.

Net: a real but much narrower 3.14-only, undeclared-interpreter, non-CI, fail-closed diagnosis residual that is already documented with its fix — low, not medium, and not real as stated.
